stem: During an end-of-shift check, at a patient's request, a DEA-registered pharmacy is asked to transfer an unfilled electronic MS Contin prescription once to another DEA-registered retail pharmacy. What pathway applies?

choices.text: Print the electronic prescription and transfer the paper image by fax if its alternate trigger can be documented.
Transfer it repeatedly while no quantity has been dispensed.
Have technicians at both pharmacies complete the transfer without pharmacist communication.
Use the one-time pharmacist-to-pharmacist electronic transfer pathway if Massachusetts law and all federal conditions are satisfied.
Treat the transaction as a Schedule II refill at the receiving pharmacy.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'Use the one-time pharmacist-to-pharmacist electronic transfer pathway if Massachusetts law and all federal conditions are satisfied.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Print the electronic prescription and transfer the paper image by fax.' would require that federal transfer rules allowed the electronic prescription to be converted out of electronic form. The decisive cue appears in 'During an end-of-shift check, at a patient's request, a DEA-registered pharmacy is asked to transfer an unfilled electronic MS Contin prescription once to another DEA-registered retail pharmacy. What pathway applies?'.

What pathway applies?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.B: 'Transfer it repeatedly while no quantity has been dispensed.' would apply only if the federal pathway permitted more than one transfer; 'During an end-of-shift check, at a patient's request, a DEA-registered pharmacy is asked to transfer an unfilled electronic MS Contin prescription once to another DEA-registered retail pharmacy. What pathway applies?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.C: 'Have technicians at both pharmacies complete the transfer without pharmacist communication.' would apply only if the rule did not require direct pharmacist-to-pharmacist communication; 'During an end-of-shift check, at a patient's request, a DEA-registered pharmacy is asked to transfer an unfilled electronic MS Contin prescription once to another DEA-registered retail pharmacy. What pathway applies?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.D: 'Use the one-time pharmacist-to-pharmacist electronic transfer pathway if Massachusetts law and all federal conditions are satisfied.': supported by electronic prescriptions.
choice_analysis.E: 'Treat the transaction as a Schedule II refill at the receiving pharmacy.' would apply only if transfer of an unfilled electronic prescription created refill authority; 'During an end-of-shift check, at a patient's request, a DEA-registered pharmacy is asked to transfer an unfilled electronic MS Contin prescription once to another DEA-registered retail pharmacy. What pathway applies?' states otherwise.

related_facts: morphine (MS Contin) is used for severe and persistent pain requiring extended opioid treatment; it is federal Schedule II and Massachusetts Schedule II.

At a patient's request, an unfilled electronic Schedule II through V prescription may be transferred once between DEA-registered retail pharmacies if allowed by state law, kept electronic, unaltered, and communicated directly between pharmacists.
